dedupe_keys.name: organisation of service delivery in us metropolitan areas solid waste management savas 1970s icpsr 7487

description: This study is the solid waste part of a 1970s research programme on how public services were organised in US metropolitan areas, led for this service by E. S. Savas and archived at the Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR). The four sister projects, on fire protection, police, public health and solid waste, shared one frame: the 200 Standard Metropolitan Statistical Areas that had under 1.5 million people in the 1970 Census and lay within one state. A limited set of variables was collected for all 200 areas, and more detailed data for samples of areas, for every local unit and every agency or firm delivering the service, such as who collected refuse, how it was paid for and at what cost. FIPS and revenue sharing codes allow linking across the four studies and with other data. The collection dates to 1974 and 1975, with some series from 1966. The files are available to download from ICPSR; access terms are those of ICPSR and the metadata states no licence. Caveats: the data are about fifty years old and useful mainly as a historical baseline, and documentation is scanned. Simulation uses: historical comparison of public, contract and private collection arrangements in service cost and organisation models. Related records: the Italian municipal cost panel (data-italy-municipal-solid-waste-cost-panel) is a modern cost series.
